Connor Zary is out (knee surgery) and has missed the last 16 games.

Kevin Bahl is out for the season and has missed the last 3 games. Joel Hanley has taken his spot beside Šimon Nemec. That pair has had 36% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 38:37 together, down from 46% with Bahl.

Martin Pospíšil has started killing penalties: on the ice for 31% of the team’s shorthanded time in 19 games, up from 2% last season.

The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 10 games cover only 28% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the third-lowest in the league (a typical team: 42%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.

Igor Chernyshov is on injured reserve and has missed the last 10 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters. Michael Misa has taken his spot beside Will Smith and Macklin Celebrini. That line has had 44% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 52:56 together, down from 60% with Chernyshov.
Alexander Wennberg is day to day, reported after he played in their last game. He is a top-six forward.

story.head: The Sharks give up shots, and the Flames take them
paras: The Flames already played in San Jose once this season and left with a 2-1 win on Nov 2. The Flames (8-10-1) lost 3-1 to the Rangers on Wednesday, and the Sharks (8-11-2) lost 3-2 in a shootout to Pittsburgh the same night. This is a Pacific Division matchup, with the Flames sixth (tied for 25th in the NHL) and the Sharks fifth (tied for 23rd). The Pacific has been the weakest of the four divisions so far.

The Flames take a lot of low-quality shots (32nd) and take more penalties than they draw (31st). As for the Sharks, they do a lot of their shooting from distance (2nd lowest) and ice the puck a lot (32nd). They also give up a lot of shots (31st), so the Flames are likely to get plenty of pucks to the net against them. San Jose has scored 2.43 goals a game, the fourth fewest in the league. Both teams like to play fast, especially the Flames (2nd), so expect an open game.

Joel Farabee (7 G / 10 A / 17 P in 19 GP) leads the Flames in scoring, and Matt Coronato (4 G / 11 A / 15 P in 19 GP) isn’t far behind. The Sharks’ scoring runs through Macklin Celebrini (8 G / 15 A / 23 P in 19 GP), who has seven points in his last five games.

Dustin Wolf (3-5-1 / .869 SV% in 9 GS) has struggled for Calgary so far, but will likely start. Yaroslav Askarov (5-8-1 / .894 SV% in 14 GS) is in line to start for San Jose. Askarov has a .925 save percentage in five starts against the Flames, well above his usual .886. Don’t read much into it: a goalie’s record against one team rarely holds up.
